papers.relied_on: V27 scored row 50 D1 and S assuming the 2004 ADA/APA/AACE/NAASO consensus monitors glucose, lipids and weight and uses no insulin or C-peptide measure (earlier project files had only secondary summaries).
papers.full_text_shows: Table 3 (monitoring protocol) lists personal and family history, weight (BMI), waist circumference, blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose and a fasting lipid profile; baseline fasting glucose is read as pre-diabetes 100-125 mg/dl and diabetes 126 mg/dl or more, with repeat glucose at 3 months and annually. No insulin, C-peptide, HOMA or OGTT is recommended for monitoring. Insulin appears only as mechanism and research text (higher fasting and postprandial insulin on olanzapine and clozapine; clamps and IVGTT as research needs). Children: height, weight and BMI percentile only.
papers.quote: Patients treated with olanzapine and clozapine have higher fasting and postprandial insulin levels than patients treated with FGAs, even after adjusting for body weight.
papers.key_numbers: Table 3 baseline items: history, BMI, waist, blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose, fasting lipids. Glucose cut-offs 100-125 and 126 mg/dl (fasting). Weight gain of 5% of initial weight: consider switching the SGA. Immediate care for glucose 300 mg/dl or more or below 60 mg/dl.
papers.role_in_work: Negative evidence: a US consensus (adult and child) whose monitoring protocol uses glucose, not insulin; also the US comparator for the CAMESA-based row 50.
papers.design: Consensus development conference statement (expert panel, literature review), 2004.
papers.population_and_size: Patients on second-generation antipsychotics; no study sample.
papers.measure_type: none for monitoring (fasting plasma glucose only); fasting and postprandial insulin mentioned as a mechanism observation only
papers.quality_note: Two-column PDF extraction interleaves the columns and loses some symbols (for example beta in 'beta-cell'); the table is partly scrambled but the item list is readable. The conference was supported in part by educational grants from AstraZeneca, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Janssen, Eli Lilly and Pfizer; several panel members declared industry grants or honoraria. Old (2004); APA 2020 not re-read here.

papers.relied_on: Rows 9 and 27 scores assumed that the consensus covers evaluation but names no C-peptide test (S1 D3 1; V14 and V20 corrected to 2 because Guidance Statement 2.4 names 'endocrine reserve' and no assay); D2 and D1 were scored 1 on the same basis.
papers.full_text_shows: Fasting glucose and HbA1c are the initial tests (Statement 2.1, 83 percent top agreement), a 75 g OGTT is the follow-up (2.2); pancreatogenic diabetes is separated from type 1 and type 2 by islet antibodies, clinical insulin resistance and an absent pancreatic polypeptide response (2.3), not by C-peptide. Statement 2.4 says endocrine reserve and functional beta-cell mass 'should be performed' for TPIAT; the supporting text states that functional beta-cell mass can be estimated from serum C-peptide during an OGTT or a mixed-nutrient meal test, and that glucose-potentiated arginine insulin or C-peptide testing may be more accurate but is not routinely available. Research recommendations ask whether C-peptide and insulin during an OGTT discriminate beta-cell function or insulin resistance, whether metabolic tests of islet hormone secretion distinguish the three diabetes forms, and whether the arginine C-peptide response predicts islet yield; no outcome data are given for any of them.
papers.quote: Assessment of pancreatic endocrine reserve, and importantly that of functional beta-cell mass, should be performed as part of the evaluation and followup for TPIAT.
papers.key_numbers: Agreement for Statement 2.4: A 45%, B 20%, C 10%, D 18%, E 8% (the lowest top-category agreement of the statements; the A-E legend (Table 1) is not in the extracted text). Statement 2.3 (PP response): A 39%. Statement 2.1: A 83%. Statement 2.2: A 69%.
papers.role_in_work: Only guideline-type source for TPIAT beta-cell reserve (row 27) and for the 3c classification question (row 9); governs D3 for both rows.
papers.design: Consensus meeting (PancreasFest 2012) using a GRADE-grid style process, electronic voting on a 5-point agreement scale, after a systematic review.
papers.population_and_size: Patients with recurrent acute or chronic pancreatitis; voting attendees only, number not in the extracted text.
papers.measure_type: stimulated C-peptide (OGTT or mixed-nutrient meal) named for beta-cell mass; arginine-stimulated insulin or C-peptide named but not routine; fasting insulin mentioned once as 'may be helpful to document hyperinsulinemia'; no C-peptide for classification
papers.assay_or_platform: none named; Table 3 (test protocols, Boost 12 ounces for the meal) is missing from the extracted text
papers.quality_note: Text is clean; tables are missing. Consensus on narrative evidence, no accuracy figures. Conflict-of-interest statement not found in the extracted text.

papers.relied_on: Row 46 scores assumed national expert criteria with C-peptide as criterion 3 of 3, no accuracy data for the C-peptide cut-offs, and no US adoption (S2/V14 D3 1-2, V15 D2 1, V17/V18 D1 3, V16 D4 2).
papers.full_text_shows: The 2012 report revised only the HbA1c cut-off (below 8.7 percent NGSP, from 382 fulminant and 122 classic type 1A patients: sensitivity 100 percent, specificity 97.5 percent for 8.9) and added an HLA comment. For C-peptide the committee states that it did not revise the cut-offs and that the data are 'not shown'. Criterion 3 needs urinary C-peptide below 10 ug/day, or fasting serum C-peptide below 0.3 ng/mL AND below 0.5 ng/mL after intravenous glucagon (or a meal) at onset; all three criteria are required. The 2004 screening criteria use only ketosis/ketoacidosis within a week and plasma glucose of 16.0 mmol/L or more, with no C-peptide.
papers.quote: we concluded that it was not necessary to revise the cut‐off value for the serum and urine C‐peptide levels
papers.key_numbers: HbA1c (NGSP) mean 6.8% in 382 fulminant patients, below 7.0% in 70.2%; cut-off 8.7% (NGSP). C-peptide: urinary <10 ug/day; serum fasting <0.3 ng/mL (<0.10 nmol/L) and <0.5 ng/mL (<0.17 nmol/L) after glucagon or meal. Pancreatic enzymes raised in 98%.
papers.role_in_work: Source of the only C-peptide cut-offs for fulminant type 1 diabetes (row 46).
papers.design: Expert committee re-evaluation of diagnostic criteria using submitted patient records (nationwide registry), 2012.
papers.population_and_size: 382 newly diagnosed fulminant type 1 patients and 122 classic type 1A patients (HbA1c analysis only); C-peptide data not shown.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (urinary 24 h, fasting serum, glucagon- or meal-stimulated serum)
papers.quality_note: Clean text, very short report. Authors state the criteria are used 'not only in Japan, but also worldwide' without evidence of adoption by a body outside Japan. The same text says undiagnosed fulminant disease 'directly results in the death of the patient', but the screening criteria it keeps do not use C-peptide.

papers.relied_on: V14 D7 for row 35 cited it for the GCK-testing branch (prevalence and referral numbers); the insulin-based part (first-trimester HOMA-IR) was the part scored.
papers.full_text_shows: No insulin, C-peptide or HOMA measure at all. 4 of 31 tested women had GCK-MODY (minimum prevalence 0.5 per 100 GDM among 776). The proposed pregnancy criteria (NSC) are fasting glucose 5.5 mmol/L or more on the antepartum OGTT and prepregnancy BMI below 25 kg/m2; sensitivity 75 percent and specificity 96.1 percent using minimum prevalence; 6.1 percent of GDM cases (n = 4,415 database) would be referred for GCK testing. Antepartum HbA1c did not separate GCK-MODY from GDM (5.6 vs 5.3 percent, P = 0.9).
papers.quote: antepartum HbA1c has limited value in differentiating GCK-MODY from standard GDM
papers.key_numbers: 776 GDM women; 63 with suggestive postpartum OGTT; 31 genotyped; 4 GCK-MODY; NSC sensitivity 75%, specificity 96.1%; 6.1% referred vs 14.2% with standard criteria.
papers.role_in_work: Supports the glucose-based GCK branch (a) of row 35 only; not an insulin or C-peptide use.
papers.design: Cohort from a single hospital GDM database (Sydney) with targeted genetic testing; projection on a larger database.
papers.measure_type: non-insulin (fasting and OGTT glucose, HbA1c); no insulin or C-peptide
papers.assay_or_platform: GCK sequencing and MLPA; glucose and HbA1c methods not described in the extracted text
papers.quality_note: Two-column extraction, readable. Only 4 cases; 32 of 63 high-risk women declined testing; selection of women by postpartum OGTT. No conflicts of interest declared.

papers.relied_on: Row 49 scores assumed a descriptive staging statement that does not recommend C-peptide for individual progression risk (S1 D3 1, V1 D3 1, V2 D2 2, V4 and V5 D1 1).
papers.full_text_shows: Stages are defined by islet autoantibodies and dysglycaemia only. C-peptide appears as a prognostic observation: stimulated C-peptide declines about 6 months before diagnosis while fasting C-peptide stays normal; a 20 percent fall from baseline carries a 47 percent 4-year risk and a 78 percent 5-year positive predictive value (ref 10); first-phase insulin response on IVGTT below the first percentile carries about a 50 percent 1-year risk (ref 69). The statement also reports that baseline insulin sensitivity, fasting insulin secretion and total postglucose insulin output were not predictive of progression (ref 72), whereas OGTT beta-cell glucose sensitivity was. It states outright that staging is for research and not for clinical practice.
papers.quote: risk screening and staging as outlined here are not recommended at this time for clinical practice
papers.key_numbers: 20% C-peptide fall: 47% risk at 4 years, PPV 78% within 5 years; IVGTT first-phase insulin below 1st percentile: 50% 1-year risk; accelerated stimulated C-peptide decline about 6 months before diagnosis.
papers.role_in_work: Consensus text for staging; supplies the only guideline-level wording on C-peptide as a prognostic marker (row 49) and the staging basis for row 30.
papers.design: Scientific statement (JDRF, Endocrine Society, ADA), narrative evidence review, 2015.
papers.population_and_size: Not applicable (review of natural-history cohorts such as DPT-1, TrialNet, DAISY, TEDDY).
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (stimulated, OGTT-derived) and IVGTT first-phase insulin as prognostic markers; fasting insulin-based measures reported as not predictive
papers.quality_note: Clean text. Dated 2015; the 'not recommended for clinical practice' sentence has been overtaken in part by later ADA Standards (autoantibody screening, staging referral), which the units cite separately. Statement of authors' conflicts not found in the extracted text.

papers.relied_on: Row 35 part (b): V15 D2 2 and D8 1 (abstract-level AUC 0.81 'in n=250 with 20 cases', independence from BMI in one model, no head-to-head comparison), V17 D1 0, V18 D1 1; S3 D2 not determinable.
papers.full_text_shows: 250 women were enrolled at 7-12 weeks; 227 were analysed (9 could not tolerate the OGTT, 14 left follow-up), 20 developed GDM (8.8 percent). HOMA-IR ROC: AUC 0.809 (95% CI 0.729-0.889), cut-off 2.08, sensitivity 90, specificity 61, PPV 18, NPV 98 percent; BMI AUC 0.723 (0.635-0.812), cut-off 25.95; weight gain AUC 0.654. HOMA-IR stayed in the logistic model with OR 1.254 (1.006-1.563, P = 0.045). Cut-offs were chosen in the same sample (no validation); a decision-tree split at 3.1 is also used; no combined-model AUC, no fasting glucose comparison (women with fasting glucose above 95 mg/dL were excluded) and no HbA1c. Weight gain (WGDP) was recorded up to weeks 24-28, so the HOMA-IR plus weight-gain tree is not first-trimester-only information. GDM was diagnosed by the two-step 50 g then 100 g test. The authors suggest weight-gain control as the action and call the sensitivity and specificity modest.
papers.quote: there is no commonly accepted HOMA-IR cutoff value
papers.key_numbers: n 250 enrolled, 227 analysed, 20 GDM (8.8%); HOMA-IR AUC 0.809, cut-off 2.08, sens 90%, spec 61%, PPV 18%, NPV 98%; BMI AUC 0.723; mean HOMA-IR 3.8 (GDM) vs 2.2.
papers.role_in_work: One of four HOMA-IR cohorts behind row 35 part (b) (first-trimester prediction of GDM).
papers.design: Prospective single-centre observational cohort, Konya, Turkey, 2014-2015.
papers.population_and_size: 227 singleton pregnancies analysed (250 enrolled), 20 with GDM.
papers.measure_type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR and QUICKI from fasting insulin and glucose)
papers.assay_or_platform: Roche Elecsys 2010 chemiluminescence insulin immunoassay; glucose by hexokinase
papers.quality_note: Text readable. The printed HOMA-IR formula (glucose in mg/L times 0.05, divided by 22.5) does not match the standard constants as printed; this may be a typesetting error, so HOMA-IR values and the 2.08 and 3.1 cut-offs may not be comparable with other cohorts. Only 20 events; cut-offs in-sample; no conflict of interest declared. The authors' cost remark (fasting glucose plus insulin 2.5 dollars vs OGTT 7 dollars) is Turkish and outside scope.

papers.relied_on: Row 13 scores (U1 D3 2, U2 D2 2 and D8 1, U3 D4 2, U4 and U5 D1 2, D5, D6, S, V7 D7 4) assumed IRIS used HOMA-IR above 3.0 only as an entry criterion, with central laboratories, no HOMA-IR-stratified analysis and no test of measurement-guided selection.
papers.full_text_shows: IRIS (n = 3,876) enrolled non-diabetic people with stroke or TIA in the prior 6 months, fasting HOMA-IR above 3.0 measured at least 14 days after the event, and reports no analysis by HOMA-IR stratum in the main text (13 prespecified subgroups, no significant interaction; Fig. 2 is not in the extracted text). Primary outcome 9.0 vs 11.8 percent, HR 0.76 (0.62-0.93) over 4.8 years. Harms: more than 4.5 kg gain in 52.2 vs 33.7 percent, oedema 35.6 vs 24.9, serious fracture 5.1 vs 3.2, discontinuation for oedema or weight gain 172 vs 51, but heart failure 74 vs 71 (P = 0.80). The authors say insulin is not globally standardized, so all testing was in central laboratories and others must adopt the IRIS assays or calibrate to them. Prediabetes was not an entry criterion (diabetes excluded by medication, repeated fasting glucose of 126 mg/dL or more, or HbA1c 7.0 percent or more; no OGTT). The text says insulin resistance is present in more than 50 percent of non-diabetic stroke or TIA patients.
papers.quote: To replicate IRIS eligibility criteria, laboratories would need either to adopt the IRIS assays or to calibrate their own results to the IRIS assays.
papers.key_numbers: N 3,876; median baseline HOMA-IR 4.7 vs 4.6; primary 175/1939 (9.0%) vs 228/1937 (11.8%), HR 0.76; progression to diabetes HR 0.48; 6.0% and 6.7% already had HbA1c 6.5% or more at baseline.
papers.role_in_work: The only randomized evidence behind row 13; HOMA-IR used as an entry criterion.
papers.population_and_size: 3,876 adults 40 or older with ischemic stroke or TIA in the prior 6 months, no diabetes, HOMA-IR above 3.0.
papers.measure_type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR from fasting glucose and fasting insulin)
papers.assay_or_platform: central laboratories; insulin assay not named in the main text
papers.quality_note: Clean text; supplement and figures not included. Funded by NINDS; Takeda donated drug and had no role in design, conduct or reporting.

proposals.reason: The 2026-10-23 correction to 2 rested on the statement naming no assay. The full text names it: in the supporting text of Guidance Statement 2.4 (TPIAT evaluation and follow-up) beta-cell mass is estimated by serum C-peptide during an OGTT or a mixed-nutrient meal, and arginine testing is described as not routine. The population (TPIAT) is covered explicitly, so clarification 14 allows 3. Kept low confidence: the recommended act is 'assessment of endocrine reserve', the C-peptide sentence sits in the evidence paragraph, and the statement had the weakest agreement (A 45%, D+E 26%). 4 is not supported (no statement that the test must precede the decision). Row 9 is not changed (its classification decision is not covered; Statement 2.3 uses pancreatic polypeptide).
proposals.quote: Functional beta-cell mass can be estimated from serum C-peptide levels determined during either oral glucose tolerance (14) or mixed-nutrient meal testing

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 43; merged-conclusion.md line 20 (GL-23 in claims.csv); UC-43

claim_issues.proposed_wording: ADA/APA/AACE/NAASO 2004 consensus, PMID 14747245, DOI 10.2337/diacare.27.2.596, full text read (local extract, 2026-10-27): the monitoring protocol (Table 3) lists history, weight (BMI), waist circumference, blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose and fasting lipids; no insulin, C-peptide or HOMA measure is recommended. Insulin appears only as a mechanism observation and as research needs.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 9, caveats column (and claim UC-09)
claim_issues.issue: Says the consensus 'diagnoses type 3c by glucose/HbA1c/OGTT and exocrine evidence'. In the full text glucose, HbA1c and OGTT detect diabetes; classification uses islet antibodies, clinical context and an absent pancreatic polypeptide response, and metabolic tests of islet hormone secretion are listed as research. The source is also recorded as abstract level.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: PancreasFest 2012 (full text): diabetes is detected by fasting glucose, HbA1c and a 75 g OGTT; pancreatogenic diabetes is separated from type 1 and type 2 by islet antibodies, clinical insulin resistance and an absent pancreatic polypeptide response; the statement recommends no C-peptide test for classification, and calls for research on whether C-peptide and insulin during an OGTT, or other tests of islet hormone secretion, help distinguish the forms.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 27, sources column (PancreasFest cited at abstract level)
claim_issues.issue: The full text shows what the consensus actually says about TPIAT reserve testing, which the row does not state.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: PancreasFest 2012, full text: Guidance Statement 2.4 says assessment of endocrine reserve and functional beta-cell mass should be part of TPIAT evaluation and follow-up; the supporting text names serum C-peptide during an OGTT or mixed-nutrient meal test, and arginine-stimulated insulin or C-peptide as more accurate but not routinely available; agreement was A 45%, D 18%, E 8%. The research recommendations say it is not known whether the arginine C-peptide response predicts islet yield or outcome. No threshold is given.

The V16 D4 reason reads the criterion as alternatives ('fasting serum below 0.3, or stimulated below 0.5, or urinary'), but the paper requires fasting below 0.3 ng/mL and below 0.5 ng/mL after glucagon or a meal, or the urinary value. The paper also says its C-peptide cut-offs were not revised and the data are 'not shown'.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Imagawa 2012 (full text): criterion 3 is urinary C-peptide below 10 ug/day, or fasting serum C-peptide below 0.3 ng/mL and below 0.5 ng/mL after intravenous glucagon (or a meal) at onset. The committee kept the C-peptide cut-offs unchanged (data not shown); no sensitivity or specificity for them is given. The 2004 screening criteria (ketosis plus glucose of 16.0 mmol/L or more) use no C-peptide.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 35, test column (a) 'fasting glucose >5.5 mmol/L in non-obese women'; caveats 'GCK cohort PMID 26109503, abstract'
claim_issues.issue: In the cohort paper the proposed criteria are fasting glucose of 5.5 mmol/L or more (not above) on the antepartum OGTT and prepregnancy BMI below 25 kg/m2 (not 'non-obese'). The paper was read in full here, not abstract only. (Whether ANZ 2025 words it differently was not checked.)
claim_issues.proposed_wording: (a) GCK testing trigger (Rudland 2015, PMID 26109503, DOI 10.2337/dc15-1001, full text): fasting glucose 5.5 mmol/L or more on the antepartum OGTT and prepregnancy BMI below 25 kg/m2; 4 GCK-MODY cases in 776 GDM women; glucose-based, not an insulin or C-peptide use.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 49, sources column (Insel 2015 'descriptive, no recommendation to test') and claim UC-49; score reasons V2/V4/V5
claim_issues.issue: The statement is more than descriptive about testing: it says staging is not recommended for clinical practice (2015). It also reports that fasting insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity and total postglucose insulin output did not predict progression, and that fasting C-peptide stays normal until about 6 months before diagnosis while stimulated C-peptide falls.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Insel 2015 (full text): stages are defined by autoantibodies and dysglycaemia; a 20 percent fall in C-peptide from baseline carried a 47 percent 4-year risk and a 78 percent 5-year positive predictive value; stimulated C-peptide declines about 6 months before diagnosis while fasting C-peptide is maintained; baseline insulin sensitivity, fasting insulin secretion and total postglucose insulin output were not predictive. The statement says risk screening and staging are 'not recommended at this time for clinical practice' (2015 wording; later ADA Standards cover autoantibody screening).

claim_issues.where: Score reason V15 D2 for row 35 ('AUC 0.81 in n=250 with 20 cases'); merged-conclusion.md line 109 and claims EV-45 (cut-offs and 'six to 14 weeks' range)
claim_issues.issue: The cohort analysed 227 women, not 250 (250 enrolled); the HOMA-IR cut-off came from the same sample; the paper reports separate AUCs for BMI (0.723) and HOMA-IR (0.809) but no combined model or fasting-glucose comparison, so 'no added discrimination tested' still holds. Gestational age at measurement was 7-12 weeks.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Alptekin 2016 (full text): 227 of 250 enrolled women analysed, 20 with GDM; HOMA-IR AUC 0.809 (95% CI 0.729-0.889) at an in-sample cut-off of 2.08 (sensitivity 90%, specificity 61%, PPV 18%, NPV 98%); BMI AUC 0.723; HOMA-IR OR 1.254 (1.006-1.563) alongside BMI and weight gain; no external validation, no combined-model AUC, no fasting-glucose or HbA1c comparison.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 13 (title 'Stroke or TIA with prediabetes/IR') and the IRIS summary in merged-conclusion.md (TRI lines)
claim_issues.issue: IRIS did not require prediabetes; it enrolled people without diabetes (no medication, repeated fasting glucose below 126 mg/dL, HbA1c below 7.0 percent, no OGTT) with HOMA-IR above 3.0. Prediabetes comes from the ADA and AACE wording, not from the trial. The other IRIS statements in the row and in TRI-02 to TRI-07 match the full text.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: IRIS (full text) enrolled non-diabetic adults with stroke or TIA in the prior 6 months and a fasting HOMA-IR above 3.0 (at least 14 days after the event); prediabetes was not an entry criterion, and 6.0 and 6.7 percent of the two arms already met HbA1c 6.5 percent or more at baseline by the 2010 ADA definition.

notes: Assumptions and failures. (1) Current scores were read from the units' JSON files; where a correction key exists the corrected value was taken (row 9 D3 2, row 27 D3 2, row 46 D1 3, D4 2, D3 1, row 13 S 1). Where several units scored one dimension the figure shown in the units was used and no combined value was computed by me. (2) C027: the A-E agreement legend (Table 1) and Table 3 are missing from the extracted text, so I did not say what 'A' means. (3) C006 and C036 are two-column PDF extracts; reading order was reconstructed and quotes are copied from the extracted lines. (4) C030 quote contains the non-breaking hyphen character as in the file. (5) No proposal for rows 9, 46, 35, 49, 50 and 13: the full texts confirm or only qualify the abstract-level assumptions. Row 13 D7 stays 4; the IRIS statement that insulin resistance is present in more than 50 percent of non-diabetic stroke or TIA patients makes the narrower HOMA-IR share in V7 (25-40 percent) look low and so makes the low end touching bin 3 less likely, a confidence note and not a score change. Row 46 S stays 1 because the 2004 screening criteria that catch fulminant cases use no C-peptide. (6) Paths to viability are not changed; for row 27 the C027 research recommendation (does arginine C-peptide predict islet yield and outcomes) names the missing evidence. (7) Optional lead: C027 Statement 2.2 evidence says a fasting insulin 'may be helpful to document hyperinsulinemia' in chronic pancreatitis with suspected insulin resistance; no use-case row exists for it and no data are given. (8) Tool calls: counted by hand about 41 (1 read, about 38 bash, 2 writes), at or just over the stated limit of 40; the over-run came from scoring-file lookups.
